title: Sevilla 1-1 Real Betis: Salas snatches late derby draw
subtitle: A dramatic stoppage-time equaliser from Kike Salas ensured the spoils were shared in El Gran Derbi.
paragraphs: Kike Salas' last-gasp equaliser rescued a point for Sevilla as the derby spoils were shared in a 1-1 draw with Real Betis.
Salas netted in the first minute of second-half stoppage time to send the home fans into raptures at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan.

Sevilla were by far the dominant force in the first half, with Lucas Stassin whipping a dangerous right-footed ball through the corridor of uncertainty for the first real chance of the contest, but while it beat Alvaro Valles, it also evaded both Ruben Vargas and the lunging Felix Correia.
Stassin then found himself in behind after a clever pass, only to see his right-footed effort comfortably gathered by Valles.
The Betis goalkeeper was called into action again shortly before the break, getting down well to deny Vargas from just outside the area as Sevilla continued to probe for the opener.
However, despite being dominated in the first half, it was Betis who found the breakthrough five minutes after the restart.

Antony was afforded far too much space to drive forward, and with time to unleash a shot, the Brazilian saw his left-footed effort take a wicked deflection off Lucien Agoume, leaving Odysseas Vlachodimos wrong-footed.
Vargas looked to inspire a response with a fierce volley from distance, but Valles got his body behind the effort.
Antony should have doubled Los Verdiblancos' advantage when he met Abde Ezzalzouli's inviting cross, but Vlachodimos stood firm to deny the winger from point-blank range.
Substitute Giorgi Kochorashvili tried his luck from a central free-kick, forcing Valles to tip the ball over his own crossbar as Sevilla searched for a way back into the contest.
Gabriel Suazo came within inches of an equaliser, thundering a left-footed effort from a tight angle against the angle of post and bar, but Betis' luck eventually ran out.
Salas found himself high up the pitch and unleashed a piledriver from outside the area that flew beyond the otherwise faultless Valles and into the net.
While Betis failed to collect all three points, they still have just two defeats to their name this season, one of which came against a near-flawless Barcelona side.
With a five-point cushion over fifth-placed Real Sociedad, Manuel Pellegrini's team can afford to dream of a Champions League push this season.
However, Betis rode their luck for large periods of El Gran Derbi, particularly in the first half, and were ultimately punished for failing to see the game out in stoppage time.
The underlying numbers also show that Sevilla, who sit sixth, were well worthy of at least a point.

Sevilla recorded 2.21 expected goals compared to Betis' 0.55 xG and outshot their rivals 25 to six, suggesting Betis will need to offer more going forward if they are to maintain their lofty position.

Even so, Betis are now unbeaten in their last five away La Liga matches (W2 D3), although they fell agonisingly short of recording three consecutive away clean sheets in the competition for the first time since October 2022.
